items.problem: Linked shared-content sources ($(SharedContentDir) + <Link> <Compile> items) are never materialized into the WinUI 3 project, so every type defined in shared content is unresolved (CS0234/CS0246) and the whole app fails to build.
items.evidence: migration-score.json winui_build_error CS0234 'SDKTemplate.Logging' / CS0246 LogView+logger types; UWP csproj has 15 <Compile Include="$(SharedContentDir)\cs\Logging\..."> + <Link> items.
items.root_cause: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 copies only files under -Source; SDK-style default globbing can't see out-of-cone linked sources, and the skill never told the agent to materialize them.
items.change: Added bootstrap section 1b: parse the UWP .csproj for <Compile/Page/Content/None/EmbeddedResource Include> items carrying a <Link>, expand the MSBuild expression ($(MSBuildThisFileDirectory), [MSBuild]::GetDirectoryNameOfFileAbove, $(prop)), and copy each into the project cone at its link path — skipping any path the scaffold already provides (protects App.xaml/App.xaml.cs/MainWindow). Harvested files are added to the copied set so they get namespace-rewrite + triage + TODO seeding. Reported in the BOOTSTRAP COMPLETE summary.
items.expected_effect: Shared helper classes (e.g. SDKTemplate.Logging) compile; CS0234/CS0246 for shared types disappear.
items.falsifiable_check: On re-run, bootstrap prints 'Linked shared sources : N harvested'; dotnet build no longer reports CS0234 'SDKTemplate.Logging' or CS0246 for LogView/*Logger; Shared\Logging\*.cs exist under the target.

items.problem: Windows.Web.Http vs System.Net.Http ambiguity (CS0104) plus the IHttpFilter.SendRequestAsync consequence (CS0535) were undocumented.
items.evidence: migration-score.json: CS0104 ambiguous HttpClient/HttpRequestMessage/HttpResponseMessage; CS0535 AddAuthorizationHeaderFilter does not implement IHttpFilter.SendRequestAsync.
items.root_cause: On WinUI 3 both HTTP stacks are in scope; the skill's only CS0104 guidance covered XAML namespaces. Switching to System.Net.Http types to resolve CS0104 breaks IHttpFilter (defined against Windows.Web.Http) → CS0535.
items.change: Added a 'CS0104 HttpClient/HttpRequestMessage/HttpResponseMessage ambiguous' subsection under Common build errors: pick one stack per file, keep Windows.Web.Http (qualify or alias) for IHttpFilter/HttpBaseProtocolFilter/AdaptiveMediaSource code, with a callout that CS0535 on IHttpFilter.SendRequestAsync is the downstream symptom and the member types must stay on Windows.Web.Http.
items.expected_effect: Agent resolves the ambiguity by qualifying to Windows.Web.Http and keeps IHttpFilter signatures intact.
items.falsifiable_check: On re-run of a Windows.Web.Http sample, no CS0104 on HttpClient/HttpRequestMessage/HttpResponseMessage and no CS0535 on IHttpFilter.SendRequestAsync.

items.problem: csproj guidance under-emphasized linked shared sources, risking either ignoring them or re-adding <Compile Include> on top of the default glob (duplicate-item errors).
items.evidence: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md > Project File Updates listed <Compile Include> only as 'drop'.
items.root_cause: Under-emphasis: no distinction between UWP-only csproj markers (drop) and linked shared source content (must be materialized).
items.change: Added a callout in Project File Updates that <Link>ed shared sources are auto-harvested into the cone by the bootstrap and must NOT be re-added as <Compile Include> on top of the default glob.
items.expected_effect: Agent does not paste <Compile Include> back in (avoids duplicate-item errors) and trusts the harvested files.
items.falsifiable_check: On re-run, no MSB3105/duplicate-item build errors from re-added <Compile Include> lines; agent relies on harvested shared sources.
